answer_reviews.evidence: Both subparts agree with the blind solution: the fixed locus is the entire alpha plane, and setwise invariant lines are precisely containing or normal lines. The necessity proof chooses an off-plane P whose distinct image P' lies on the invariant line, forcing that line to follow PP' normal to alpha. The answer separates pointwise fixation from setwise invariance. No numeric units apply; free geometric classification must not receive an exact text key.

Provides a natural spherical droplet model and technical finite right-cylinder/box models, with correct center/axial reflection planes. Explicit idealization and real-object defects avoid claiming exact symmetry of every real object. Notes allow other valid examples. This open example-generation task is ungraded, not artificially constrained to a text key.

The X to X' to Y' to Y chain stays in Phi. Because reflection is involutive and preserves midpoints, the image of midpoint O is O' and O' bisects XY. Thus every X has its O'-symmetric mate in Phi; central inversion is involutive, so this proves setwise symmetry. Uniqueness gives O'=O and the fixed locus gives O in alpha. This is the blind conjugation proof expressed synthetically. The note correctly identifies extra plane uniqueness as unnecessary. A proof is appropriately ungraded.

The answer uses a different valid witness from either blind source construction or authored choice. For A=(0,0,0), B=(0,3,0), C=(1,0,1), D=(1,0,-1), det(AB,AC,AD)=6, so it is nondegenerate. Directly squared edge lengths are 9,2,2,11,11,4 as displayed. Their incident multisets distinguish A and B from each other and from C,D, forcing A,B fixed and C,D exchanged. Reflection z=0 provides existence and is the unique perpendicular-bisector reflection of C,D; a plane cannot fix all four vertices. Hence exact uniqueness is proved rather than merely asserted. Construction/existence/proof is appropriately ungraded.

answer_reviews.evidence: Proves both required properties: the common plane direction makes a transverse line intersect beta, and a beta-normal line would also be alpha-normal by theorem 19, contradicting slant incidence. It does not silently reduce 'slant' to merely 'not perpendicular'. This matches the blind proof, requires no units, and is appropriately ungraded.

Both subparts match the blind contradiction/common-normal argument. The first excludes coincidence and parallelism, forcing intersection. The second excludes a shared perpendicular for intersecting planes. The note correctly avoids inferring that a must be slant to beta: it may be contained in or parallel to beta. All conclusions are displayed, no units apply, and open classification/reasoning is appropriately ungraded.

The translation proof is a valid independent route to the same blind result. Translation by AB sends alpha to the unique parallel plane through B, namely beta. The image D' of C lies both in beta and on the common normal line CD; uniqueness of their intersection gives D'=D and vector CD=AB, so lengths are equal. It covers coincident normal lines without assuming a nondegenerate quadrilateral. This proof task is appropriately ungraded and has no numerical unit to specify.

The seed's closed-segment conditions force M-B-A and M-C-D. The answer correctly obtains MA=17 cm, BC=sqrt(13^2-12^2)=5 cm, BC parallel AD and the enlargement factor MA/MB=17/12, hence AD=85/12 cm. Both requested outputs are separately labeled |BC| and |AD|, and both parts declare unit cm. Expected inputs are bare numeric LaTeX 5 and fraction 85/12, not display prose or unit strings; the exact rational avoids premature decimal truncation. Numeric-equivalence grading is semantically appropriate. Runtime parser/input validation is intentionally deferred to the parent.

The answer fully realizes both source tasks. Equal distances to C,D put A,B,O in the perpendicular-bisector plane pi; nondegeneracy makes them noncollinear. With P,M the AC/BC midpoints and E the CO midpoint, EP parallel OA and EM parallel OB force the normal slice PME; the D-side construction gives NQF. E,F are distinct CD quarter-points, and exactly the three edges incident to C or D cross each respective slice. The reflection fixes A,B, swaps C,D and maps P->N, M->Q, E->F, proving whole-section congruence. The optional SSS equalities PM=NQ=AB/2, PE=NF=AO/2 and ME=QF=BO/2 are also correct. All vertex labels and corresponding sides are consistent. This construction/proof task is ungraded, with no fake automatic position or proof judgment.
